cleared.check: Task 2, halts other than REVERT, constructed with eth_call and state overrides against the deployed PoolManager of each of the 21 networks (HaltProbe.sol, halt.py, halt_fix.py in the work directory). A probe frame writes its own transient slot and then either (variant 1) enters unlock and, in the callback, mints 5 claims, syncs a currency and writes a second slot, or (variant 2) syncs a currency outside unlock, and then halts. Kinds: REVERT as control, INVALID (0xfe), stack overflow by unbounded internal recursion, out of gas by an endless loop, and, under STATICCALL, a TSTORE by the probe, PoolManager.sync and PoolManager.unlock. A later frame then reads the unlock flag, the nonzero delta count, the probe's delta, the synced currency and reserves with exttload (src/Exttload.sol:10-15), the probe's claim balance and the probe's own two slots. In a second test the call into the probe was given every gas value from 1 up to the first value at which it succeeds (step 1 over the last 8,000 gas below that value and step 9 or coarser below), so that out of gas falls at every reachable point inside the PoolManager, the callback and the balanceOf staticcall: 362,827 attempts, 362,743 of them failing. The first successful gas is 39,572 on most networks, 39,324 on Monad, 81,193 on MegaETH and 281,586 on Tempo, where creating a storage slot costs more.
cleared.result: No leak on any network: 0 failed attempts read back a write. The successful controls show every written slot (synced currency 0x00000000000000000000000000000000c0ffee16 and reserves 1000 plus the attempt id, the probe slots 7 and 9), so the reads can see a write that survives. A static call into PoolManager.sync or unlock fails at its first TSTORE (src/libraries/Lock.sol:13, src/libraries/CurrencyReserves.sol:29-30) and writes nothing, so a static violation cannot leave a write by construction. PoolManager never catches a failed callee: the hook call bubbles the failure (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:134-137), token and native payouts revert (src/types/Currency.sol:48-52 and 73-83), and the callback is a plain high level call (src/PoolManager.sol:110), so a halt in any of them reverts the whole unlock. On MegaETH the simulated call runs on the RPC node, not the closed sequencer (OPCODES.md, MegaETH row).
cleared.source: eth_call with state overrides on the rpc URL of each network in state/networks.json, 2026-11-25, results in cycles/016/theme-revert-rollback-mined.work/raw/halt_all.json and raw/halt_fix.json; https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-1153 (a reverted frame undoes its transient writes and those of inner calls); src/libraries/Lock.sol:10-27; src/PoolManager.sol:104-114, 279-288

cleared.check: Task 2, call depth 1024: how deep a chain of self calls with all gas gets under a 30,000,000 gas eth_call, and what the PoolManager does when a call it makes fails for depth.
cleared.result: The chain stops at depth 358 on 18 networks, 357 on Tempo and 291 on MegaETH (98/100 forwarding), well short of 1,024, because each level keeps 1/64 of the gas: (63/64)^1024 is 9.9e-8, so reaching depth 1,024 needs about 10^10 gas at the top, and (98/100)^1024 is 1.0e-9 on MegaETH. Where depth were reached, the failed outgoing call returns 0 without halting the PoolManager frame, and every outgoing call of the PoolManager turns a failure into a revert (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:137, src/types/Currency.sol:52 and 83, src/PoolManager.sol:110), so the unlock reverts and its transient writes go with it.

cleared.check: Tokens the node implements natively, inside frames that revert or halt: the probe TokenRollbackProbe.sol was placed by state override at the PoolManager address of Base, Tempo, Celo and Arc so that it holds what the PoolManager holds, and it transferred 1 unit of Base B20 OUSD (0xB2000000000000000000002fEb517dFeC7415344) and AMDc (0xb2000000000000000000000d8ce462e99ee7a47b), Tempo TIP-20 pathUSD (0x20c0000000000000000000000000000000000000), the CELO ERC-20 face (0x471EcE3750Da237f93B8E339c536989b8978a438) and the Arc USDC face (0x3600000000000000000000000000000000000000) inside a frame that then reverted, hit INVALID, overflowed the stack or ran out of gas, and under STATICCALL; on Celo and Arc also a native value transfer read back through the face. A take or settle inside an undone frame is only safe if these precompile balances roll back with the transient delta.
cleared.result: All eight cases roll back: in every halted or static case the sender and recipient balances of both faces read afterwards equal those before, and the successful control moves one unit (raw/token_rollback.json). Ethereum USDC was run as a bytecode control with the same result. On Arc a native transfer of 1 wei lowers the sender's face balance by one face unit (10^12 wei) and the recipient's face shows 0, because the face reports floor(balance / 10^12); this is the rounding of the existing two-face hazard (F-100, F-108), and one face unit is worth 10^-6 USDC, far below the gas of a round.

cleared.check: Task 3, ERC-4337 bundles on every network, which join several users' operations into one transaction. Whether transient storage is cleared between operations, and a mined bundle in which two unrelated senders' operations both called the PoolManager. Bundles among PoolManager transactions (UserOperationEvent of EntryPoint 0.6, 0.7 and 0.8, aa.py): Base 5,610 PoolManager transactions in blocks 61,965,599 to 61,973,598, 170 bundles, 1 with two or more senders, 0 where two senders reached the PoolManager; Ethereum 6,000 PoolManager transactions in blocks 26,489,705 to 26,490,154, 65 bundles, 1 with two or more senders, 0 where two senders reached the PoolManager; Polygon 6,000 PoolManager transactions in blocks 97,904,651 to 97,919,750, 223 bundles, 2 with two or more senders, 0 where two senders reached the PoolManager; Arbitrum One 6,000 PoolManager transactions in blocks 527,245,513 to 527,333,512, 59 bundles, 0 with two or more senders, 0 where two senders reached the PoolManager; Optimism 6,000 PoolManager transactions in blocks 159,986,660 to 159,993,159, 0 bundles, 0 with two or more senders, 0 where two senders reached the PoolManager; Robinhood Chain 3,000 PoolManager transactions in blocks 122,805,462 to 122,811,461, 64 bundles, 0 with two or more senders, 0 where two senders reached the PoolManager; Unichain 3,000 PoolManager transactions in blocks 64,830,284 to 64,836,583, 0 bundles, 0 with two or more senders, 0 where two senders reached the PoolManager.
cleared.result: Transient storage is not cleared between operations: EIP-1153 discards it only at the end of the transaction, and the EntryPoint runs every operation as a nested call of the one handleOps transaction. The unlock flag and the deltas cannot pass from one operation to the next, because unlock clears the flag and requires every delta to be zero before it returns (src/PoolManager.sol:104-114). Only the synced currency and reserves can. No mined bundle with two senders' PoolManager calls was found: the only multi-sender bundles have one operation that reaches the PoolManager, for example Base 0x61046bec99fa8dc23efda3e63f0bedc7e18b233fb191c09ff26edfbaced2b66c (EntryPoint 0.6, senders 0x0de04d745d88dc18e7c519f1935a3e27917e795f and 0xcbeebaf9d1f94a6678dad25e14afd2fb042bc579, only the second calls unlock, sync, settle, swap, mint and take). sync needs no unlock and leaves the synced currency and reserves in transient storage until a settle by anyone resets it (src/PoolManager.sol:279-288, 349-364). A first party that leaves a sync gains nothing: settle credits msg.sender or the named recipient (src/PoolManager.sol:300-307, 364), so a credit from a stale sync goes to the second party. The second party can lose only through its own integration. If it pays native value without its own sync, settle reverts with NonzeroNativeValue (src/PoolManager.sol:356, recorded as F-071). If it pays an ERC-20 without syncing first, it is credited the balance change since the first party's sync: a take of its own after that sync makes the subtraction at src/PoolManager.sol:360 revert or under-credits it, and unlock then reverts with CurrencyNotSettled (src/PoolManager.sol:112). No path moves another user's pool balance or claims.

cleared.check: Task 3, Tempo type 0x76 batched and sponsored transactions: does transient storage survive between the calls of a batch, and can two unrelated users share it?
cleared.result: The calls of a batch share one transient map: execute_batch takes one checkpoint before the first call, runs every call with the transaction's caller as sender, rolls the checkpoint back when any call fails and keeps all writes otherwise (handler.rs execute_batch, lines 1284-1366 on main). Every call has the same msg.sender, so only the signer's own calls share the state, and a fee sponsor pays fees without becoming a caller. Two unrelated users cannot share a batch, so no mined transaction of that kind can exist; zone portal batches are the one Tempo context that joins parties and are recorded as F-135. sync needs no unlock and leaves the synced currency and reserves in transient storage until a settle by anyone resets it (src/PoolManager.sol:279-288, 349-364). A first party that leaves a sync gains nothing: settle credits msg.sender or the named recipient (src/PoolManager.sol:300-307, 364), so a credit from a stale sync goes to the second party. The second party can lose only through its own integration. If it pays native value without its own sync, settle reverts with NonzeroNativeValue (src/PoolManager.sol:356, recorded as F-071). If it pays an ERC-20 without syncing first, it is credited the balance change since the first party's sync: a take of its own after that sync makes the subtraction at src/PoolManager.sol:360 revert or under-credits it, and unlock then reverts with CurrencyNotSettled (src/PoolManager.sol:112). No path moves another user's pool balance or claims.

cleared.check: Task 3, HyperEVM system transactions: are they joined with user transactions so that transient storage is shared?
cleared.result: No. The public replay client builds the environment for each system transaction and each signed transaction separately, calls transact once per transaction and commits state after each (run.rs lines 99-168 and the loop over system_txs at line 217). Each system transaction is its own transaction and starts with empty transient storage, so nothing joins it with a user's PoolManager call. The validator itself is closed (F-120).

cleared.check: Task 3, OP Stack deposit transactions: are deposits joined with other transactions?
cleared.result: No. The deposit specification processes each deposit as a transaction of its own with its own receipt, sender and gas accounting, and the revm journal used by op-reth clears transient storage in commit_tx, discard_tx and finalize at the end of every transaction (inner.rs lines 141, 174 and 207) and restores it on checkpoint_revert (line 622). A deposit therefore shares no transient state with a user's PoolManager call.

cleared.check: Task 3, Arbitrum retryable redeems, automatic and manual: does a redeem run inside the transaction that scheduled it?
cleared.result: No. A redeem is returned by TxProcessor.ScheduledTxes as a new transaction (tx_processor.go lines 924-957) and the block processor applies it after the originating transaction as a transaction of its own, keeping the group's redeems and checkpoint (block_processor.go lines 91 and 126-159), and every transaction passes through StateDB.Prepare, which resets transient storage before code runs (state_transition.go lines 735-736). A redeem shares no transient state with the transaction that created or redeemed it.

cleared.check: The reference interpreter tools/opdiff/pyevm.py, used by earlier cycles to judge PoolManager behaviour, was extended here for whole mined transactions and gave one wrong result first.
cleared.result: pyevm.py gives a DELEGATECALL frame CALLVALUE 0 instead of the value of the calling frame (tools/opdiff/pyevm.py:205 passes 0 as value). This unit's copy (pyevm_tx.py) carries the value through and also adds block context, logs, ecrecover, modexp, EIP-7702 designators and an approximate GAS. The PoolManager build contains no DELEGATECALL (OPCODES.md, bytecode census), and the delegate calls of pmdiff6.py run inside the unlock callback, which the PoolManager calls without value, so no earlier PoolManager comparison is affected.

leads.question: Extend the whole-transaction reference rerun (pyevm_tx.py) with models of the node-implemented contracts it stopped at, TIP-20 tokens on Tempo, B20 tokens on Base and ArbGasInfo (0x6c) on the Nitro chains, and rerun the reverted-then-completed unlock transactions it could not run, starting with Tempo 0xba5c0224452fbe54eb5198aad0bba1cf5a4b86db6e40eb4f4265024a79bdfa27.
leads.why: On these networks the producer evidence for rollback of an undone frame rests on the node's own trace for the transactions that use precompile tokens, which are the pools whose token state the reference cannot follow. Constructed calls show that B20 and TIP-20 transfers roll back, so the expected answer is no difference.

leadResults.answer: Answered on eight of the eleven networks the task names, with a reverted and then completed unlock on seven. Mined transactions in which an undone unlock is followed by an unlock that completes exist on Tempo (0xba5c0224452fbe54eb5198aad0bba1cf5a4b86db6e40eb4f4265024a79bdfa27), BNB Smart Chain (18 of 1,490 traced), Avalanche (0x95051c7cb718ea109a63be8c55a7b51d7e1306def99fd5b7e59b35308f0c25a6), Arbitrum One (0x33050352c9e5c462c3f86d454679d163a822785ba932ba6b8f3dae35c12dfd4b), Robinhood Chain (2), OP Mainnet (2) and Base (6), and in every one the later unlock completed. Unichain had undone frames that were extsload reads only. 31 such transactions were rerun whole in the reference interpreter from parent-block state, 20 of them with a reverted and then completed unlock: all 641 PoolManager frames end the same way and all 770 changed storage slots end equal. Arc, Elysium and Celo remain open: Arc and Elysium serve no trace method to the public, and Celo's tracing endpoints have pruned the state of every PoolManager transaction within reach. Halt kinds other than REVERT leak nothing on any of the 21 networks in 362,827 constructed attempts.
